solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hit performance by current politician

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A review of a politician's smash-hit turn, as if an MP had gone on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here means 'next to', so the pieces sit together; the order is set by the answer, with current and politician placed before the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a blow or collision, the force of one thing striking another.

clue.text: Mobilises poorly, accepting pawn is hopeless

indicators.note: the letters of MOBILISES are put together badly, so rearranged

parts.note: P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player's sorry verdict: the pieces are badly deployed and even giving up a pawn cannot save the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'pawn' look like part of the story, but it is just the letter P added to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impossible is hopeless: there is no chance of it.

clue.text: Show underwear with nothing covering bottom

parts.note: PANTS, with its bottom letter S replaced

explanation.surface: An order to show off your underwear with nothing on your backside, a cheeky bit of exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb (display the underwear) but is the noun. A panto (pantomime) is the British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and cross-dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for pantomime, a British Christmas stage entertainment, so a show by example.

clue.text: Shy and hollow little laugh

parts.note: to shy is to throw, or chuck

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A timid person's weak, empty little laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective for the laugh, but it is the verb meaning throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a quiet, suppressed laugh.

clue.text: Periodically, news reporters love coffee

indicators.note: take the letters at regular intervals: every second one

explanation.surface: Journalists, it seems, love their coffee from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' works only on 'news', not the whole phrase, which a solver might try first.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small, strong black shot made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Dismisses retracted line at end of letter

indicators.note: drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to fire is to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: An employer sacks someone, takes back what they wrote, and ends the letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' in the surface sounds like correspondence; in the definition it is a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a line of a printed letter.

clue.text: Are bull flies cause of mild rash?

indicators.note: the letters fly about, landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether the flies around a bull give it a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' reads as the insects pestering a bull; it is the verb, telling the letters to scatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, German measles, is a viral illness whose symptom is a mild rash.

clue.text: Record of performance scratched on outside of motor

parts.note: to score a surface is to scratch it

explanation.surface: A record of how a car's paintwork was scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's scratched paintwork suggests a damaged car, but 'performance' points to sport: a card on which a round or innings is recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorecard records how a player or team performed.

clue.text: Unlock old enclosure

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pen is an animal enclosure

explanation.surface: An instruction to unlock an old pen or pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the gate of an enclosure, which is where the answer belongs too.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to unfasten a door or gate so it can swing wide.

clue.text: Two mates finally dropping down the hatch

indicators.note: each word loses its final letter

parts.note: china = mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'; two of them, each losing its last A

explanation.surface: Two friends at the bar, one after the other falling down drunk into the hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a mate is a china. Chin-chin and down the hatch are both toasts said before drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is a toast, like 'down the hatch'.

clue.text: Bureaucrat training new parking attendant

parts.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking

explanation.surface: An official in charge of training a new car park attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking attendant' reads as one job, but it splits into P and USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A penpusher is a clerk or bureaucrat doing dull paperwork.

clue.text: Penniless guy changes side

parts.note: BLOKE, with its L to be switched
the other side: R for right replaces L for left

explanation.surface: A man with no money switches political sides.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloke is British slang for a man. 'Side' means left or right, so BLOKE's L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: without a penny to your name.

clue.text: Present royal fellow less well, faced with absurd cost

indicators.note: the letters of COST are made nonsense of, so rearranged
the anagram goes in front of the rest

explanation.surface: A royal who has taken ill is confronted with a ridiculous bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb, but it is the gift. A stocking filler is a small Christmas present put into a child's stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of present: a small gift tucked into the Christmas stocking a child hangs up.

clue.text: Company information is possibly dealt with there

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters: DEALT with THERE

explanation.surface: A remark that company data is perhaps handled at some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words of fodder together.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterhead carries a company's name, address and other details at the top of its notepaper.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute or a difficulty
a person's offspring, in the formal legal word

explanation.surface: Difficult children, the parents' lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' for offspring is formal and legal, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a problem and a person's children.

clue.text: Carol free, wanting some time, to choose

parts.note: to free is to let out; the T goes
T = time, removed from LET OUT

explanation.surface: Someone named Carol is at liberty but, short of time, must make a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb meaning sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: to pick one person or thing from a group for special attention.

clue.text: Charts do not reveal cases blown apart

indicators.note: the letters of APART are blown about, so rearranged

parts.note: to hide is to not reveal

explanation.surface: Maps and charts that keep secret cases that have been blown wide open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like a noun (legal cases) but is the verb: HIDE cases the jumbled APART, giving HI(TPARA)DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated name for the weekly ranking of best-selling pop records, the charts.

clue.text: Rotate bed to accommodate a renegade

indicators.note: the bed takes the A inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Turn the bed around to make room for a deserter.
explanation.walkthrough: The A sits inside COT, giving CO(A)T.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts to the other side, a renegade.

clue.text: Proprietor's path runs around rolling hill

parts.note: R = runs, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
a down is a rolling chalk hill in southern England

explanation.surface: A proprietor's footpath winding around a rolling hill on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is'. LANE + R makes LANER, which goes around DOWN: LAN(DOWN)ER. The Downs are the rounded grassy hills of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor in the particular sense of someone holding an estate or acres.

clue.text: Inappropriate milieu for after-school networking?

parts.note: OB = old boy; old boys network after leaving school
a scene is a milieu or setting

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a certain setting is unsuitable for old pupils making contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old boy network' is the British web of contacts among former pupils of a school; OB SCENE is the place for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, at its strongest: offensive to decency, grossly unsuitable.

clue.text: Trainee section of designated activity is over

indicators.note: the answer is a section of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A trainee's allotted task has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies across the gap between the two words and runs right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee, especially in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Prudence raising hundred in sale

parts.note: AUCTION with its C lifted out

explanation.surface: A careful bidder putting a hundred up at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: AUCTION already holds the C; moving it to the top of this down entry gives CAUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Caution is prudence, care to avoid risk.

clue.text: Mysterious event left drilling company with spotted work surface

parts.note: a kitchen counter is a work surface

explanation.surface: An oil company leaves an unexplained incident behind, drilling through a stained worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: A close encounter is a UFO sighting or contact with aliens, as in the film Close Encounters of the Third Kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A close encounter is a mysterious sighting of an alien craft.

clue.text: Social media platform stops recording about foreign resident

parts.note: X is the platform formerly called Twitter

explanation.surface: A social media site shuts down a recording about an expat.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside the reversed tape: E(X)PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) lives abroad, a foreign resident.

clue.text: Start to cheat, breaking honest agreement

indicators.note: take the first letter of cheat
breaking a word splits it open

explanation.surface: Beginning to cheat means breaking an honest deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a moral about deals; 'agreement' at the end is the definition, not part of the story about cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific agreement: one between enemies to stop fighting for a time.

clue.text: Creep uncovered financial records

indicators.note: the covering first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts; drop L and R

explanation.surface: A sneaky person has exposed secret accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' reads as a noun, a nasty person; it is the verb, as in to edge forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to move forward slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Lots of people went by car, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a crowd moving together, like a herd of cattle

explanation.surface: Crowds of people who travelled by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' allows for other vehicles: one drives a bus or a lorry too.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving crowd, and drove is also the past tense of drive.

clue.text: Page with space for truism

parts.note: latitude is space or freedom to act

explanation.surface: A page with room left for a trite remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Latitude here is scope or leeway, not the map line.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a remark so obvious and overused it says nothing.

clue.text: Request agreement, in French first

explanation.surface: A plea for an agreement, first drafted in French, the language of diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: French is the old language of diplomacy, which is why an agreement drafted 'in French' feels natural in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an earnest plea or appeal.

clue.text: Where ownership details can be checked, to be sure

definitions.text: Where ownership details can be checked
definitions.meaning: a deed is the legal document recording who owns a property, and the details are in it

explanation.surface: Where to look up property records, just to be sure.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer as IN DEED, the place ownership is written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an emphatic 'certainly', and literally inside the title document of a property.
